primary_route: Developmental monocular/bilateral/dark-rearing and reverse-occlusion factorial proposal.

checks.reason: Core exposure duration/intensity, stimulus timing and cortical acquisition/response settings remain a list to select later, without executable quantitative settings or a sufficiently specified calibration-to-setting procedure.

Optical/stimulus and response calibration is named, but quantitative acceptance-to-action thresholds or a concrete derivation of tolerances for eye isolation, delivered contrast and mapping reliability are absent.
Contrasts and clustering are recognized, but the actual response/distribution model, assumption diagnostics and specified multiplicity policy remain incomplete.
Age, exposure dose and stimulus-parameter exploration has no bounded candidate grid or objective range-selection/search-stop rule before locking.
Troubleshooting does not explicitly connect technical changes to a revised frozen procedure and fresh independent confirmation; ordinary initial pilot separation is insufficient.
No complete raw-animal/unit-to-output manifest with calibration records, exact analysis versions/settings and all exclusions/deviations is specified.

The experimental MD effect is declared its own positive control and absence mandates halting, making the hypothesis unfalsifiable under the stated protocol. There is also no operational upstream functional comparator or sham delivery control.
No quantitative dominance estimator, weak-response threshold or deprived-eye alignment rule is given despite randomizing eye side; named indices alone are not executable measurement definitions.
Pupillary/light-response checks do not independently validate matched retinal/thalamic patterned input. No independent confirmation cohort or operational orthogonal cortical validation is specified.

Age dependence does not distinguish instruction from permissive maintenance, and the maintenance hypothesis is assigned no-deprivation-effect predictions without justification. The mechanism discriminator is not identifying.

Two onset categories cannot establish a bounded critical-period curve; dark-reared-versus-normal endpoint differences alone do not measure prolonged plasticity. The final claims exceed the measured contrasts.
